title: Standby LED blinks 2 times
shortDescription: Backlight inverter or LED driver fault on Bravia TVs.
fullDescription:
On Sony Bravia TVs the standby red LED encodes self-diagnostic codes. A two-blink pattern typically points to a backlight system failure - either the LED driver board, backlight strips, or a short on the panel power rail.

The TV usually shows a brief flash of picture before shutting off, or audio plays with no image. The set then enters a protection mode and refuses to start until the fault clears.

causes.cause: Failed LED backlight strips inside panel
Defective LED driver / power supply board

fixSteps.title: Confirm blink count
fixSteps.instruction: Count blinks across multiple cycles - 2 blinks = backlight, 6 = main board, 7 = panel.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 2 minutes, hold power button 30 seconds, replug.

fixSteps.title: Service backlight
fixSteps.instruction: Disassembly and LED replacement is best left to a technician.

whenToCallPro: Backlight replacement requires opening the panel - call a pro unless you have experience.

faq.a: Usually yes, but power supply issues can produce the same pattern.

title: Main board / power failure
shortDescription: Sony 6-blink code indicates main board or B+ power rail fault.
fullDescription:
Six red blinks on a Bravia indicates the main processing board has lost communication with the power supply, or a critical voltage rail has failed.

The TV will not start beyond the standby LED. Sometimes a firmware corruption can mimic this code; a hard reset clears those rare cases.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 5 minutes, hold power 60 seconds, replug.

fixSteps.title: USB recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Download firmware from Sony support to USB, follow recovery steps.

fixSteps.title: Board replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If recovery fails, main board needs replacement.

whenToCallPro: Almost always requires professional diagnosis - boards are model-specific.

faq.q: Can I replace the main board myself?
faq.a: Yes if you can find an exact part number match, but pairing may require service mode.

title: HDMI input shows no signal
shortDescription: TV cannot detect a source on the selected HDMI port.
fullDescription:
Bravia displays 'No Signal' when the connected device is not outputting video, the HDMI handshake fails, or the wrong input is selected.

This is one of the most common Bravia complaints, especially with PlayStation 5 4K/120Hz HDMI 2.1 ports.

fixSteps.title: Cycle inputs
fixSteps.instruction: Press Input, switch to source, then back.

fixSteps.title: Try different cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use Ultra High Speed HDMI cable for 4K/120 sources.

fixSteps.title: Enable Enhanced format
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > External inputs > HDMI signal format > Enhanced for that port.

whenToCallPro: Only if HDMI port is physically damaged.
videoSearchQuery: Sony Bravia no signal HDMI fix

faq.q: Why does PS5 show no signal?
faq.a: Enable Enhanced format on the HDMI port and use an Ultra High Speed cable.

title: HDCP authentication failed
shortDescription: Copy protection handshake between TV and source did not complete.
fullDescription:
When HDCP fails, the TV cannot display protected content (Netflix, Blu-ray). It typically shows a black screen with an error or just goes black after a few seconds.

Causes include incompatible HDCP versions, AVR pass-through issues, or recently changed HDMI signal format settings.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle chain
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug TV, AVR, and source for 60 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Toggle Enhanced format
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > External inputs > HDMI signal format - try Standard then Enhanced.

fixSteps.title: Bypass AVR
fixSteps.instruction: Connect source directly to TV to isolate AVR.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed - usually solved by reseating cables and power cycling.

faq.a: Digital copy protection that must authenticate before video plays.

title: Android TV / Google TV software update failed
shortDescription: OTA update did not complete, often due to network or storage issues.
fullDescription:
Sony Android TVs and Google TVs occasionally fail to install updates. Causes include weak Wi-Fi, full system storage, or interrupted downloads.

The TV is usually still functional, but features may be degraded until the update completes.

fixSteps.title: Switch to Ethernet
fixSteps.instruction: Wired connection is more reliable for large updates.

fixSteps.title: Clear storage
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Apps - uninstall unused apps and clear caches.

fixSteps.title: USB update
fixSteps.instruction: Download firmware from Sony support, copy to USB, install.

whenToCallPro: Only if USB recovery also fails.

faq.a: USB updates preserve settings; factory reset will not.

title: Netflix network connection error
shortDescription: Netflix cannot reach servers from your Sony TV.
fullDescription:
Netflix error NW-2-5 indicates the TV cannot establish a connection to Netflix servers. It can be a DNS issue, a network outage, or that the app needs a re-sign-in.

This appears across many Bravia models running Android TV / Google TV.

fixSteps.title: Test internet
fixSteps.instruction: Open browser/YouTube to confirm general connectivity.

whenToCallPro: Not necessary - this is a network/software issue.

faq.q: Does NW-2-5 mean my TV is broken?
faq.a: No - it's a network or app connectivity issue.

title: PlayStation 5 VRR causes black screen flicker
shortDescription: Variable Refresh Rate causes intermittent signal loss with PS5.
fullDescription:
Bravia XR sets paired with PS5 sometimes suffer signal dropouts when VRR is enabled. The screen flashes black for a second under fast frame-rate changes.

Firmware updates have largely fixed this, but it still appears with certain games or HDMI cables.

fixSteps.title: Replace HDMI cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use a certified Ultra High Speed HDMI cable.

fixSteps.title: Disable VRR
fixSteps.instruction: PS5 Settings > Screen and Video > VRR Off as a workaround.

videoSearchQuery: Sony Bravia PS5 VRR black screen fix

faq.a: No - update firmware first; VRR works well after recent updates.

title: Sony remote control not responding
shortDescription: TV does not react to remote button presses.
fullDescription:
Sony's voice remotes use Bluetooth pairing for voice and IR for basic controls. When pairing breaks, the voice/Google Assistant button stops working but power/volume may still respond via IR.

Full failure usually means the remote needs re-pairing or new batteries.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair remote
fixSteps.instruction: Hold Home + Volume Down for 5 seconds near TV.

fixSteps.title: Reset TV BT
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Remotes & accessories > Forget remote, then re-pair.

whenToCallPro: Never needed - replace remote if failed.
videoSearchQuery: Sony TV remote not working pair

faq.q: How do I know if it's the remote or TV?
faq.a: Use the Sony TV mobile app as a backup remote to test.

title: Vertical lines across display
shortDescription: Colored vertical lines indicate panel or T-CON failure.
fullDescription:
Vertical lines on a Bravia almost always trace back to a failed T-CON board, broken ribbon cable, or damaged panel.

This is rarely repairable economically on smaller sets - the panel often costs more than a new TV.

fixSteps.title: Test on multiple inputs
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm lines appear on every input including the menu.

fixSteps.title: Reseat T-CON cables
fixSteps.instruction: Open back, reseat ribbon cables to T-CON.

fixSteps.title: Quote panel cost
fixSteps.instruction: Get quote - panel replacement is rarely worth it.

whenToCallPro: If reseating cables doesn't help - panel work needs experience.

faq.a: Often not - compare repair quote to replacement cost first.

title: Audio lags or leads video
shortDescription: Lip-sync mismatch with HDMI ARC/eARC or apps.
fullDescription:
Lip sync issues on Bravia happen most often via ARC/eARC to a soundbar or AVR. Apps like Netflix and Hulu can also drift if processing is heavy.

The A/V sync setting and Auto Sound Mode usually correct it.

fixSteps.title: A/V sync adjust
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Display & Sound > Audio output > A/V sync.

fixSteps.title: Switch to optical
fixSteps.instruction: If ARC misbehaves, optical can be more reliable.

videoSearchQuery: Sony TV audio out of sync fix

faq.q: Why is sync worse on Netflix?
faq.a: Streaming apps add encoding delay - use the A/V sync slider.

title: Bravia Sync / CEC not working
shortDescription: Connected devices don't auto-power or respond to TV remote.
fullDescription:
Bravia Sync is Sony's HDMI CEC implementation. When it fails, devices don't power on with the TV, the TV remote doesn't control the soundbar, or input switching breaks.

The most common cause is CEC being disabled on either end after a firmware update.

fixSteps.title: Enable Bravia Sync
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Channels & Inputs > External inputs > Bravia Sync settings.

fixSteps.title: Enable CEC on partner
fixSteps.instruction: Each brand calls it different (Anynet+, Simplink, Viera Link).

fixSteps.title: Re-handshake
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle both devices with TV last to power on.

faq.a: Yes, but each brand has its own name for it - enable on both.

title: Streaming app crashes or fails to open
shortDescription: Apps freeze on splash screen or kick back to home.
fullDescription:
Sony Android/Google TV apps occasionally crash on launch due to corrupted cache, full storage, or app-side updates that conflict with the TV's OS version.

Clearing cache and data usually solves it without reinstalling.

fixSteps.title: Clear cache + data
fixSteps.instruction: Same menu - Clear cache then Clear data (you'll re-sign in).

fixSteps.title: Reinstall
fixSteps.instruction: Uninstall and reinstall from Play Store.

videoSearchQuery: Sony Google TV app won't load fix

faq.a: Clearing data signs you out; clearing cache does not.

title: Netflix UI-800-3
shortDescription: Netflix app shows error UI-800-3 on Sony TV, usually cache-related.
fullDescription: Error UI-800-3 indicates a cache problem between the Netflix app and its servers. Most cases clear with a sign-out, app reload, or network reset. Persistent errors may need firmware update or factory reset.

causes.cause: Stale app cache or expired session token
Outdated TV firmware or app version

fixSteps.title: Restart TV
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug TV for 60 seconds then power back on to clear memory.

fixSteps.title: Sign out and back in
fixSteps.instruction: Open Netflix, sign out, then sign back in to refresh the session token.

fixSteps.title: Check network
fixSteps.instruction: Run network test in TV settings; reboot router if speeds are low.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Support > Software Update; install any pending update.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall app
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the Netflix app from the home screen and reinstall from the store.

whenToCallPro: Only if errors persist after factory reset.

faq.q: Is UI-800-3 a TV hardware fault?
faq.a: No — it is an app/network error and clears with sign-out, reinstall, or firmware update.

title: 4K120 dropouts on PS5
shortDescription: HDMI handshake/HDCP failure on Sony TV; use Enhanced format and certified cable.
fullDescription: HDMI 2.1 4K120 DROP indicates the TV failed to negotiate HDCP/EDID with the connected source. Common with 4K/120 Hz, eARC receivers, and long passive cables. Cycle power on both devices and try a certified Premium High Speed HDMI 2.1 cable.

causes.cause: HDCP handshake failure between source and TV
Source set to output unsupported format (4K120, Dolby Vision)
eARC/CEC conflict with AVR in chain

symptoms: Black screen with audio or no signal

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle the chain
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug TV, source, and AVR for 2 minutes; plug TV in first, then source.

fixSteps.title: Swap HDMI cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use a certified Ultra High Speed HDMI 2.1 cable under 2m.

fixSteps.title: Try a different HDMI port
fixSteps.instruction: Move source to another HDMI input; label the port for 4K/120 if needed.

fixSteps.title: Match source output
fixSteps.instruction: Set the source to 4K60 RGB to test, then raise resolution/refresh.

fixSteps.title: Toggle Enhanced Format
fixSteps.instruction: TV settings > External Inputs > HDMI Signal Format > Enhanced.

whenToCallPro: Replace HDMI board if multiple ports fail with a known-good cable.

faq.a: For 4K120/VRR/eARC, only certified Ultra High Speed HDMI 2.1 cables reliably pass the handshake.

title: eARC No Audio
shortDescription: eARC connection drops audio to AVR on Bravia.
fullDescription: When eARC is enabled the TV should pass Atmos to the AVR over HDMI 3. If audio drops, the eARC handshake is failing — usually CEC, AVR firmware, or cable.

fixSteps.title: Toggle eARC
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Sound > eARC Mode > Off, then On.

fixSteps.title: Use eARC cable
fixSteps.instruction: Plug certified Ultra High Speed cable into HDMI 3 (eARC).

faq.a: On most Bravia models, HDMI 3 is the eARC port — check your manual.
